Just saw the first real reviews, especially the Tom's Hardware one. My takeaways:

Performance is about what realistic expectations at it at between a 290 and a 390

Uses too much power

Way too hot

Overall. Good buy at $200. Once you get to $250 where it mostly is right now you can do better for just a bit more with a 390/390x.

EDIT: I wrote the above on mobile. Here is some more info about what I am seeing about the power. Tom's shows it pulls 90 watts out of the PCIe interface that is rated for 75 watts max. Not good at all. (Since found out that this only applies to 2.0 and prior PCI-e so i am clear but others may not be). It is easily correctable by having 2x6 pin. And it runs hot on the stock cooler, which OEM will correct in newer versions. Problem is that the price/performance ratio dies quickly over $250 in the US and those two corrections will easily add another $30 to the price. At $280 for the 8GB, this is competing with the 390 and 970 directly. At $200-230 the 4 GB is a steal, but only once the OEM versions come out with more power connectors and better cooling solutions.

Uses too much power

Compared to what? Its power draw is about half of the 390 if I read right. That's a drastic improvement.

In my opinion, the price to performance ratio is incredible. At $200, falling between a 290 and 390 with half the power consumption of a 390 is a steal. Video cards have been prohibitively expensive the past few generations, and this card should allow a lot of cash-strapped gamers get quality, current-gen upgrades or help potential PC gamers finally make the leap.

I'm stoked, I need a laptop for school, but I want a nice desktop. I could go out and buy almost everything no problem except a video card. I'm hoping AMDs new line will let me double up finally. I'm also willing to bet there are others in the same boat as me.

From what limited reviews I have seen so far it seems like an extremely solid entry level card. And I think this is exactly what AMD was aiming for. I think it is a foundational piece upon which they can stand in todays market. It is not meant to be the god card. It is meant for the masses. Most people that respond here will have very powerful systems I think, so it will likely take a little bit of flak. But I would ask for people to step back and give it a couple weeks while the dust settles. I personally own a 780 and run Linux. It is not currently enough of an upgrade but it is enough for me to stop and take a long hard serious look at it.

I think for $200 it could open up VR to the many more people. It should also keep pressure on the GTX970 so prices stay down for the near future. I'd say it's an overall win for the PC community and hopefully will boost VR capability. I think it also gives AMD a path for efficiency to make it down to the 150-170 price point in the future if needed.

Anyhow, my hope is that it does well so more PCs will be VR capable should a much cheaper Gen2 headsets and Chinese knock offs start entering the market. Then VR for everyone!
